title: Ghost and Deadline
premise: Lior Sandoval, a peace-delegation interpreter, is approached by a woman named Vess who claims he saved her life seven years ago — a debt he has no memory of incurring. As she draws him into a plot against the network that secretly trained him, Lior discovers his missing memories were surgically curated: he was never a bystander, but an asset. The peace talks are a cover for the network's final consolidation of power, and the extraction flight at dawn is the only window to destroy them. Lior burns the network from inside its own summit, chooses exile over the flight, and ends owning his past at the cost of the belonging he always craved.
about_author: Beatrix Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where languages were weapons and minutes were currency. She writes thrillers about people fluent in other people's lies.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During a stalled ceasefire negotiation, a woman named Vess corners him at the hotel bar and repays a debt he doesn't remember earning, leaving a key and a warning. Emotional beat: uncanny unease — the first crack in a life built on rules.

chapters.title: Simultaneous
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He interprets a session where delegates say one thing and mean another, and realizes he's been translating the network's intentions, not the parties'. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: The Key Opens a Year
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The key opens a storage locker containing files on himself: training reports, psychological profiles, and a seven-year-old photo of him with Vess. Emotional beat: vertigo; the self he trusted becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Vess Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She watches Lior through a borrowed camera feed, recalling the real debt — he did save her, and the network erased it from him deliberately. Emotional beat: guilt braided with cold purpose.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He confronts his handler, Marek, who gaslights him smoothly and reassigns him to the summit's inner circle — a promotion that is clearly a cage. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging offered by the very people betraying him.

chapters.title: The Delegation Destined to Fail
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He decodes a mistranslation he himself delivered years ago that sabotaged the last peace process. Emotional beat: horror at discovering his voice was the weapon.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Borrowed Memory
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She lays out the network's method: recruit, train, excise, deploy — and shows Lior the clinic where his memories were cut. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger who was himself.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns the Dawn
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. He meets Corvain, the network's architect, who offers him full restoration of his memories in exchange for delivering Vess. Emotional beat: temptation — the price of wholeness is betrayal.

chapters.title: What Vess Owes
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Her backstory: she was the network's first extraction, and Lior's forgotten kindness is the only proof she was ever a person to them. Emotional beat: tenderness weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Marek tests Lior's loyalty by forcing him to mistranslate a live session; Lior complies and hates himself. Emotional beat: shame deepening into quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: The Summit Floor
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The peace summit opens; he works the room, mapping which delegates are assets. Emotional beat: adrenaline and clarity — the failure is choreographed, and he can read the score.

chapters.title: A Room With Two Doors
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She infiltrates the summit as a press attaché and meets Lior in person for the first time in seven years. Emotional beat: recognition — two people pretending not to know each other, meaning it.

chapters.title: Marek's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior steals Marek's ledger of assets and finds his own name flagged for termination after dawn. Emotional beat: cold fear converting into commitment.

chapters.title: The Extraction Flight
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She reveals the dawn flight: the network's board, its archives, and its escape route in one plane. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Corvain's Offer, Repeated
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Corvain restores a fragment of Lior's memory as a down payment — and it's the moment he saved Vess. Emotional beat: the past returns as proof he was always capable of loyalty.

chapters.title: Double Translation
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the summit's closing session, Lior mistranslates on purpose — feeding the network a false script while signaling the delegates. Emotional beat: mastery reclaimed; his voice, his rules.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She and Lior breach the network's archive to copy the ledger of every asset ever made. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in danger; belonging, briefly, real.

chapters.title: Marek Closes the Door
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Marek catches them; Lior talks his way past him using the handler's own protocols, then locks him in the archive. Emotional beat: the student outgrowing the cage.

chapters.title: Dawn Is a Choice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Corvain offers a final bargain: full memory, a new identity, a place at the table. Lior refuses and triggers the archive upload to every delegate and journalist on site. Emotional beat: the climax — power refused at the moment it's finally offered.

chapters.title: The Flight Leaves Without Them
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The board's plane departs into a storm of exposure; arrests begin on the tarmac as the ledger goes public. Emotional beat: catharsis — the machine dismantled by its own schedule.

chapters.title: What Was Taken, Returned
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A defector clinic offers to restore everything the network cut. Lior reads the file and chooses partial restoration — keeping the man he became. Emotional beat: reconciliation with an edited self.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Unattached
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Months later, Lior interprets a small, honest negotiation in a border town; Vess waits outside. Emotional beat: quiet belonging, chosen rather than trained — memory as something you build, not recover.
